name: Filling to the Crown, Crossing the Brow-Bridge
previous_label: Chaturanga Dandasana — Four-Limbed Staff (asana framing, retired 2026-10)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: tayāpūryāśu mūrdhāntaṃ bhaṅktvā bhrūkṣepasetunā | nirvikalpaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā sarvordhve sarvagodgamaḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
dharana.rendering: Having quickly filled [the body] up to the top of the head with that [breath-power], and having broken through by means of the 'bridge' made by contracting the eyebrows, make the mind free of thought-constructs; then, in what is above all, the all-pervading arises.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: fill the mūrdhānta with prāṇic energy and cross it with the bridge-like contraction of the eyebrows. Singh adds that the esoteric bhrūkṣepa technique 'was a closely guarded secret among the mystics and is now practically lost'. The Mystery Within's own rendering reads the 'breaking' as suspending the breath while concentrating at the ājñā cakra.
dharana.technique_name: Filling to the Crown, Crossing the Brow-Bridge

checked_against: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y5 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)
numbering_variants.previous_draft: The previous draft of Door 008 used Wallis Y8 = verse 34. Under Singh, verse 34 is dharana 11 (Door 011).

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 31 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: body filled up to the crown
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a column filled with breath-power up to the head, a crossing at the brow, and an opening above. Observe-only: studied, not drilled.
geometry.svg_hint: a column filling upward, a small bridge drawn at the brow, an open space above; drawn faint to signal observe-only
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Breach (observed)
reaction.summary: School metaphor: a filled, pressing state breaks open into pervasion. A picture for understanding, not a class exercise. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.cue: Natural breath only. No forced retention, no rapid filling of the breath, no contraction of the brow. Observe-only door.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Study the verse; let the face and brow stay soft while you do
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Understanding the verse's sequence: fill, cross the brow-bridge, free the mind of constructs
attention.secondary: Noticing and softening any tension in the forehead while reading

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Having quickly filled [the body] up to the top of the head with that [breath-power], and having broken through by means of the 'bridge' made by contracting the eyebrows, make the mind free of thought-constructs; then, in what is above all, the all-pervading arises.
adiyogi.method_summary: Classical method: rapidly filling the body to the crown with breath-power, breaking through with a contraction of the eyebrows, and making the mind free of thought. Observe-only in this school because it relies on forceful breath-filling and deliberate brow contraction, and is read by some as suspending the breath. For practice, use Door 011 (attention inside the skull, eyes closed) or Door 003.

honesty.disclosure: Door 008 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 8 (verse 31) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 008 is dharana 8, verse 31. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.

historical/observe_only: Relies on fast, forceful filling of the breath and deliberate contraction of the brow; some read it as suspending the breath. Taught as text to understand, not as a class drill.
Numbering correction: the previous draft used Wallis Y8 = verse 34 and taught that verse here. That material moves to Door 011.

legacy.disclosure: Linking [retired posture] to VBT dharana 008 is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not a claim of ancient one-to-one canon.
legacy.notes: Serial school index pairs D-008 with method index 008 (Wallis yukti 8 / verse 34). Shared teaching hook: gradual steadiness of mind under sustained effort. Edition variance: some popular lists number a later illusion/painting verse as dharana 8; this draft follows the school's sibling pattern (dharana N ≈ early yukti N).

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Forceful breath-filling, breath suspension and sustained brow contraction are not taught by this school. They can bring headache, dizziness or light-headedness. Do not attempt them from a written description. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: [retired posture] (knees on the floor, same elbow-rib geometry) or stay in [retired posture] if wrists or shoulders complain. [retired posture] is always a valid exit.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Ease or skip if wrists, elbows, shoulders, or low back complain; do not force the shoulders below the elbows or collapse the midsection.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

safety.observe_only_note: Forceful breath-filling, breath suspension and sustained brow contraction are not taught by this school. They can bring headache, dizziness or light-headedness. Do not attempt them from a written description.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 008: filling to the crown and crossing the brow-bridge. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 8, verse 31. This door is observe-only.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make, and no drill. Sit or lie comfortably while we look at the verse. Its map: a body filled to the crown, a bridge at the brow, an opening above.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the face and forehead stay soft. Eyes open. Attention on understanding.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath only. No forced retention. No rapid filling.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Hold the sequence in mind: fill, cross, free the mind. Notice if the brow tightens while you read, and let it soften.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a filled, pressing state breaks open into pervasion. A picture, not an exercise.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 31: fill to the crown with breath-power, break through by the brow-bridge, free the mind of constructs, and the all-pervading arises. Observe-only here. For practice, use Door 011 or Door 003.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Take an easy breath. Relax the forehead. Move on when ready.
